devices.roomTypeNotes: KING STUDIO FAMILY — 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116 (KS Connecting), 118 (KS Acc. Mod / Connector): PTAC-1. Both sources agree — M301 says PTAC-1 at all 16 first-floor rooms, and M401 does not call details 03/04/05 out as PTAC-2. QQ FAMILY — 101 (QQ Wide Conn.), 103 (QQ Conn.), 105, 107, 109, 111, 113, 115: CONTESTED. M301 = PTAC-1; M401 detail 01 = PTAC-2. Exactly these 8 rooms carry the composite mark in the DB. That is an 8/8 split of MARK CONVENTION, not an 8/8 split of hardware — no sheet states that 8 rooms get PTAC-2 and 8 get PTAC-1.
devices.note: TWO DIFFERENT UNITS — SETTLED. M201 schedules PTAC-1 and PTAC-2 as separate rows with different G.E. model numbers (AZ65H12DAB vs AZ65H15DAB) and different capacities (11,900 vs 14,200 BTU/h cooling). M601 COMcheck independently lists them as two separate compliance items with different efficiencies (11.8 EER/2.86 COP vs 10.60 EER/3.5 COP). Two units, confirmed twice. WHICH ROOMS GET WHICH — NOT SETTLED on floor 1. M301 (the only M-sheet carrying floor-1 room numbers) states PTAC-1 at all 16 first-floor guestrooms. M401 states PTAC-1 on most rooms with PTAC-2 on the higher-load types and says details 01/02 show PTAC-2 — detail 01 is the QQ family, which on floor 1 is 101, 103, 105, 107, 109, 111, 113, 115. Mutually exclusive for those 8 rooms. M401 KN7 itself defers location to M301–M304 ("PTAC schedules/locations vary — refer M201 for schedules & capacity and floor plans M301–M304 for locations"), which argues for M301 governing, but M401's own detail contradicts it. NOTE ON THE MARK: no sheet prints the string "PTAC-2 / PTAC-1" — the sheets print PTAC-1 and PTAC-2 separately. The composite is the deliberate carry-both convention from packages/mechanical.md §7 (flag F4) and is what the DB prints on the 8 QQ rooms. SETTLES IT: read the PTAC tag off the M301 field set at each of the 8 QQ rooms, or read the nameplate model on the installed unit (AZ65H12DAB = PTAC-1, AZ65H15DAB = PTAC-2). The nameplate is the fastest answer and the walker is standing in front of it.
devices.verifyAtPunch: Read the nameplate: G.E., model number, 208/1/60 — record it, that alone resolves F4 for the room. Unit fully seated and level in the sleeve, secured, front cabinet/panel undamaged and flush. Operate: heat mode and cool mode both cycle from the wall control; fan hi/lo; no rattle in the chassis or against the sleeve. Confirm the unit is not sitting on top of finished carpet (KN30 = edge of PTAC ABOVE carpet tiles) and that the ST-01 stone stool over it is set, level and not bearing on the unit cabinet.

devices.verifyAtPunch: Continuous caulk joint all around the sleeve, interior and exterior faces, no gaps or shiners. Drywall closure at the PTAC-to-opening gap complete, finished and painted. devices.label: PTAC exterior louver / architectural wall grille kit (the visible exterior face at every guestroom window)
devices.qtyPerRoom: 1 per PTAC per the sheets — but see note: two sources put it in two different subcontractors' scope, so on a given room it may arrive as a PTAC accessory or as part of the window unit.
devices.where: Exterior face of the PTAC sleeve at the window wall — visible from outside the building and from the room by looking through/at the unit's outdoor section.
devices.sheets: M201 PTAC notes · M501 det.9 · M401 KN1 · A200 keyed note 8 (= AS105 keyed note 8, same text) · AS103 PTAC through-wall detail · size reference "A-601" (sheet does not exist in the issued set — RFI R-04)
devices.roomTypeNotes: Same item in all floor-1 types. No sheet varies it by room type.
devices.note: FIVE STATEMENTS, NO RESOLUTION — reported exactly as each sheet reads, not merged. (1) M201 PTAC notes: "wall sleeve kit + POLYPROPYLENE LOUVER KIT (COLOR BY ARCHITECT)" — a moulded plastic kit, colour chosen by MWT as a submittal selection. (2) M501 detail 9: "ALUMINUM ARCHITECTURAL-STYLE GRILLE FACTORY-PAINTED TO MATCH EXTERIOR WALL" — aluminium, finish applied at the factory. (3) M401 KN1: "ARCHITECTURAL WALL GRILLE FURNISHED WITH UNIT; GRILLE PAINTED TO MATCH EXTERIOR WALL (TYPICAL FOR ALL PTAC UNITS)" — furnished with the unit, painted (shop or field, not stated), matched to the exterior wall. (4) A200 keyed note 8, verbatim: "ALUMINUM FIXED WINDOW WITH THERMAL BROKEN FRAME, INSULATED GLAZING WITH INTEGRAL ALUMINUM LOUVER AT PTAC UNITS - SEE SHEET A-601 FOR SIZES." — aluminium and INTEGRAL TO THE WINDOW SYSTEM, i.e. the glazing sub's buy, not a PTAC accessory at all. (5) AS103 PTAC through-wall detail: "INTEGRAL LOUVER TO BE INSTALLED WITH WINDOW SYSTEM" — corroborates (4). So the set disagrees on MATERIAL (polypropylene vs aluminium), on FINISH METHOD (architect-selected colour vs factory-painted vs field/shop painted to match), and on SCOPE (PTAC accessory kit vs part of the window unit). Consequence: polypropylene louvers are moulded in colour and generally cannot be field-painted to an architect's colour after the fact, so M201's product and M401's paint instruction may be physically incompatible. Compounding: the size reference on A200/AS105 points to sheet A-601, which is NOT in the issued set (the set has A600 Doors and A610 Windows) — so the louver has no dimensional source either. SETTLES IT: one RFI to MWT/the M-EOR covering material, finish, colour and which sub buys it, plus the A601→A610 correction. Also confirm whether M301 Key Note 3 (corrosion-resistant ≥1/4" mesh insect screen on louvers) is meant to apply to the PTAC louver — that note is written in the combustion-air/exterior-louver context and does not name the PTAC.
devices.verifyAtPunch: From outside: louver present at every guestroom PTAC, straight, fully seated in the sleeve, fastened, blades not crushed or missing. Colour consistent room to room and matching the approved exterior colour — walk the whole elevation at once, mismatched louvers only show up in a row. Sealant at the louver-to-wall/window joint continuous. From inside: no daylight around the louver, no water staining below it. Record the material actually installed (plastic vs aluminium) on the first room and compare against the approved submittal before writing anything up.

devices.label: Interior architectural wall grille at the PTAC, painted to match the interior wall (M401 KN5)
devices.qtyPerRoom: Not resolvable from the sheets — see note. M401 carries KN1 (exterior) and KN5 (interior) as two separate keyed notes.
devices.where: Room-side face of the PTAC / sleeve at the window wall.
devices.sheets: M401 KN5 ("Architectural wall grille furnished with unit; grille painted to match INTERIOR wall") vs M401 KN1 (same wording, "EXTERIOR wall")
devices.roomTypeNotes: M401 keynotes are written as typical for all PTAC units; no floor-1 type is called out differently.
devices.note: M401 prints two nearly identical keyed notes — KN1 "grille painted to match exterior wall (typical for all PTAC units)" and KN5 "grille painted to match interior wall." The sheet does not say whether that is ONE grille whose two faces are painted two different colours, or TWO grilles (an exterior architectural louver plus a separate interior-face grille). M401's own body text reads it as one grille with an exterior face and an interior face; M401's implications line reads it as "exterior + interior wall grilles" (plural). This matters at punch because it decides whether there is a separate painted grille inside the room to inspect, and it decides a paint scope (who paints the room-side face, and in which colour). Included IN and flagged rather than dropped, because if a second grille exists it is squarely visible in a finished room. SETTLES IT: same RFI as the exterior louver — ask the M-EOR whether KN1 and KN5 describe one grille or two, and confirm who paints the interior face and to which PT code.
devices.verifyAtPunch: Look at the room-side face of the PTAC/sleeve. If a grille is present there, confirm it is fastened, undamaged and painted to match the adjacent interior wall finish (not left mill/white). If no separate interior grille is present, record that — it is the evidence that closes this flag. Either way, note what you see on the first room and apply it across the floor.

devices.qtyPerRoom: 1 per PTAC

devices.sheets: M501 det.9 · M401 KN2 · M301 General Note 6 (full-size condensate from each packaged AC unit to 2"Ø condensate riser) · AS103 PTAC detail (condensate routed through wall; termination options)

devices.qtyPerRoom: 1 per PTAC per M201's accessory sentence

Occupancy sensor function: leave the room with the door shut, confirm the unit setbacks; re-enter, confirm it recovers. Confirm the controller is hardwired and live, the faceplate is flush and level, and the wall behind it is finished and painted. Mod / Connector, the only ISA room on the floor per A100) the 48" room under M401's rule and the other 15 the 54" rooms — but see the note, that 54" is contested by four other sources.
devices.note: THE DEVICE IS SETTLED — it exists, it is 7-day programmable, it is hardwired, and the mechanical contractor furnishes it (M101 N28: the ELECTRICAL contractor furnishes, routes and installs control WIRING; the MECHANICAL contractor furnishes and installs the controls, terminates the wiring, and provides the thermostats; equal to Honeywell or factory-provided with the equipment). THE HEIGHT IS NOT SETTLED — three values across five sources. 48": A550/A552/A555 keynote 24 verbatim "HARDWIRED THERMOSTAT FOR PTAC. MOUNTED 48\" MAX TO TOP OF DEVICE"; M101 GN29 "4'-0\" AFF unless noted"; G402 note 11 "ALL CONTROLS FOR USE BY GUESTS 15\"–48\" AFF"; G400's accessible-guestroom diagram tops the control band at 4'-0". 54": M401 KN4 alone, for non-accessible rooms. 60": E101's symbol legend. M401's 54" is the outlier and the only source for it. Logged as coordination_issues.md C-03, live across all 115 rooms and an inspection item on the 7 accessible keys. DO NOT WRITE UP A HEIGHT DEFICIENCY ON THIS WALK until the RFI is answered — record the measured height instead. Confirm: hardwired and live; 7-day schedule programmable and the clock set; calls for heat and for cool and the PTAC responds within a reasonable interval; faceplate flush, level, cover plate clean; not mounted on an exterior wall if an interior wall was available (M101 N29), and if it is on an exterior wall confirm the insulated backing plate. devices.label: Aldes constant-airflow regulator at the 50 CFM ceiling exhaust inlet
devices.qtyPerRoom: NOT ESTABLISHED — see note. M305 shows one at each guestroom inlet; M305's own riser totals only account for 49 inlets against roughly 119 needed.
devices.where: At the toilet exhaust ceiling inlet, immediately behind/above the EAG-50 grille.
devices.sheets: M305 exhaust-riser diagrams EV-1…EV-7 ("CEILING GRILLE EXHAUST 50 CFM c/w ALDES CONSTANT AIRFLOW REGULATOR" at each inlet) — the ONLY source · repeated in M302/M303/M304 for the typical floors
devices.roomTypeNotes: Not varied by room type. M301 shows only risers EV-1, EV-2, EV-5 and EV-6 reaching floor 1 — which of the 16 rooms hangs off which riser is not determinable from the sheets in hand.
devices.note: The item is real and named — M305 states it verbatim at every inlet it draws, and M302/M303/M304 repeat it. What is NOT established is that there is one in every guestroom, because the only sheet that scopes them does not add up. M305's seven riser totals sum to 2,450 CFM, which at 50 CFM per inlet is exactly 49 inlets — against 115 guestrooms plus the 4 ice-machine alcoves (M201 gives EF-1 area served as "Toilet, ice machine"), roughly 119 inlets needed. M305 accounts for 41% of them. Independently, three of the four roof fans are scheduled BELOW the riser CFM assigned to them: EF-8 200 CFM against EV-1+EV-3 = 350; EF-9 300–350 against EV-4+EV-5 = 650; EF-11 400–450 against EV-2+EV-7 = 850; only EF-10/EV-6 balances at 600. Aggregate shortfall 850 CFM. Either the seven risers drawn are a partial set or the riser CFM totals are wrong, and M305 does not say which. This is the single most expensive unverified line in the mechanical package. SETTLES IT: the M-EOR reconciling the EV riser schedule against the room count and the roof-fan capacities. Until then, record presence/absence per room — 16 data points on this walk is real evidence for that RFI.
devices.verifyAtPunch: Drop the EAG-50 grille and look: is a constant-airflow regulator installed behind it, yes or no? Record per room — this is the cheapest way to generate hard evidence for the open riser/regulator RFI. If present, confirm it is the correct nominal CFM and is seated in the duct, not loose. If absent, do not assume it belongs there yet — log it, do not write it as a deficiency until the EOR answers.

devices.note: MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE READINGS. M201 schedules EF-1 as a real Panasonic FV-0511VK2 ceiling fan, 50 CFM, with remark 3 = "switch w/ room lights" and remark 5 = backdraft damper and remark 6 = off-white aluminium grille. M202, M301, M302, M303 and M304 all repeat EF-1 as the guest-toilet exhaust. But M305's riser diagrams show each guestroom inlet as a PLAIN CEILING GRILLE + ALDES REGULATOR on a central riser driven by roof fans EF-8 through EF-11 — no in-room fan anywhere. A grille-only inlet on a central riser and a dedicated in-room fan cannot both be true. PTAC exterior louver — FIVE different statements, no resolution. M201: 'polypropylene louver kit (color by architect)'. M501 det.9: 'aluminum architectural-style grille factory-painted to match exterior wall'. M401 KN1: 'architectural wall grille furnished with unit; grille painted to match exterior wall'. AS103 PTAC detail: 'integral louver to be installed with window system'. Disagreement spans material (polypropylene vs aluminium), finish method (architect-selected colour vs factory-painted vs field-painted to match), and SCOPE (PTAC accessory kit vs part of the window unit — HVAC sub vs glazing sub). Polypropylene is moulded in colour and generally cannot be field-painted, so M201's product and M401's paint instruction may be physically incompatible.

M401's body text reads it one way, M401's own implications line reads it the other. Decides whether there is a separate painted grille inside the finished room, and whose paint scope the room-side face is.

EF-1 — a real in-room Panasonic FV-0511VK2 bath fan, or a designation for a grille inlet on the central EV riser? E400's Panel A/B guestroom schedules carry no exhaust-fan circuit, which leans grille-only but is not conclusive (M201 remark 3 'switch w/ room lights' would put it on the Lighting circuit). coordination_issues.md C-06. Closable by looking behind one bath grille on this walk.

Aldes constant-airflow regulator count is not supported by its only source. M305's seven riser totals sum to 2,450 CFM = exactly 49 inlets at 50 CFM, against roughly 119 needed (115 guestrooms + 4 ice-machine alcoves). Separately, three of four roof fans are scheduled below the riser CFM assigned to them (EF-8 200 vs 350; EF-9 300–350 vs 650; EF-11 400–450 vs 850; only EF-10/EV-6 balances) — 850 CFM aggregate shortfall. Do not price 115 and do not price 49.

EAG-50 and WAG-30 are callouts in M101's designation/CFM format, NOT schedule marks. M201's Titus schedule has no row named EAG-50 or WAG-30 — its exhaust-air-grille entry is mark E (Titus PSS-DF, 24×24, 6"Ø neck, ceiling). A550 carries keynote 20 in its elevation set without the transcription naming which elevation. A552 — room 118's sheet — does not place keynote 20 anywhere at all. One wall device or two is not stated on any mechanical sheet. The architectural set places only one control device in the guest room (A55x keynote 24), which leans to one, but that is the architect's sheet and is not conclusive.

M201's Titus diffuser marks A, B, C, D, E, R and the linear A are placed in the corridor and public areas, not the guest rooms. If a walker finds a ceiling supply diffuser in a floor-1 guest room, that is unaccounted for and should be raised.

Which EV riser serves which floor-1 room is not determinable. M301 shows only EV-1, EV-2, EV-5 and EV-6 originating on floor 1 — three of the seven risers do not reach the first floor at all, yet M305 draws all seven as spanning Attic/4th/3rd/2nd/1st. Feeds directly into the Aldes/roof-fan arithmetic problem above.

M301 Key Note 3 requires a corrosion-resistant ≥1/4" mesh insect screen on louvers. That note is written in the combustion-air / exterior-louver context and does not name the PTAC louver. Whether it extends to the 115 PTAC louvers is not stated.

M301 General Note 13 permits a lined transfer duct OR a door undercut (for make-up air under 50 CFM), and M101's legend defines an undercut door at UC 1/2". No sheet places an undercut at any guestroom bathroom door — M401 shows WAG-30 instead. M502, M601 and M602 are image-based sheets (Hilti firestop UL cards; COMcheck printout) and were not text-mined. The specific Hilti UL system, annular-space limits and the COMcheck line items must be read off the source PDFs. conflicts.md §B2.3. M602's Final Inspection section is effectively the HVAC closeout list (O&M manuals, controls calibrated, duct/pipe insulation, as-builts within 90 days, air-balancing report to owner) and should be mapped to the QC tracker separately from this punch list.

M401 is Rev 04 'REVISED' 07-26-24 and is the ONLY mechanical sheet checked by RN/NS rather than AG/RN; M201 is Rev 04 08-09-24. The guestroom architectural sheets A550–A556 are Rev 4 08/09/24. Verify all of these against the live Procore set before the walk — conflicts.md §B2.4 notes the revision spread, and A100 itself carries a Rev 5 'REVISED PER RFI' dated 12/12/24 that postdates its own title-block date.

Controls scope split, for writing up deficiencies to the right sub: M101 General Note 28 — the ELECTRICAL contractor (United Electric) furnishes, routes and installs control WIRING for all mechanical systems; the MECHANICAL contractor (Iceberg) furnishes and installs the controls, terminates the control wiring, and PROVIDES the thermostats. Thermostats equal to Honeywell or factory-provided with the equipment. PTAC condensate piping is Larry's Plumbing (M401 KN2). The PTAC field-built sub-base is GC/architectural. Exterior grille/louver colour approval is MWT's.

M101 General Note 30 makes a complete Test & Balance report a required deliverable to the owner, the engineer AND local code officials — including airflow and temperature at each diffuser and grille. Every CFM reading taken on this walk (50 CFM at EAG-50, 30 CFM at WAG-30, 45 CFM OSA at the PTAC) should be reconciled against that report rather than treated as an independent judgement.

WHICH FIRST-FLOOR ROOM IS THE COMMUNICATION-FEATURES ROOM is the single highest-value unknown on this list, and it is cheap to close. Both unit matrices agree floor 1 has exactly one and that it is a King Studio, but A100 says a plain one (104/106/108/110/112/114) and G001 says a connecting one (116). Nobody has scanned A100's first-floor plan for the E500-defined "INDICATES HEARING IMPAIRED SUITE" symbol — A102 was scanned (309, 313, 316, 318), A101 and A103 were not, and A100 is not even in C-04's action list. One read of A100 at full scale, cross-checked against E501, settles the doorbell for all 16 rooms.

ROOM 118 IS THE ACCESSIBLE ROOM BUT IS NOT A COMMUNICATION-FEATURES ROOM — do not conflate them. Both matrices put 118 on the "King Studio ACC MOD, CD" row, separate from every HI row. C-04 proves the two are independent in this building: room 317 carries the ISA symbol and has zero strobes, while room 309 is a plain Queen-Queen and has three. 118 gets NO doorbell. What 118 does get, uniquely on floor 1, is the accessible reach requirement — at least one outlet AND one data connection between 15" and 48" AFF with a compliant clear floor area (A530–A533 General Note G; G402 note 11) — and two one-way viewers on the entry door.

ROOM 118 AND THE WAP — A552 is the sheet that governs room 118 and its electrical-plan keyed-note list omits kn44, while A550, A551 and A555 all carry it and kn44's own text says "TYP ALL GUESTROOMS". Either the sheet omits a keynote it should carry, or 118 genuinely has no WAP. Look at A552 view 04 at full scale before the walk.

THE WAP IS NOT DESIGNED IN THIS SET (conflict LV-2) — it appears on the A550 power & signal legend and in kn44, and NOWHERE in any E-series schedule: no count, no circuit, no cabling design, no power source. Hilton requires an approved integrator per connectedroom.hilton.com. Who designs, powers and installs it is open, and that means there is no document to punch the installation against beyond kn44's own wording.

PER-ROOM DROP COUNTS FOR THE STANDALONE DATA OUTLET ARE NOT STATED ANYWHERE (gap LV-3). The device symbols on A550/A552/A555 view 04 and on E400 are graphics, not text — A550 states outright that which symbol sits at each dimensioned point is answerable only by inspecting the drawing. Every text-based extraction will keep returning nothing. Count them off the PDF at full scale, or walk the first room with the integrator and set the standard there.

THE TV CONNECTION HAS TWO MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE OPTIONS AND NEITHER IS SELECTED (kn47) — option A (non-smart TV: coax AND CAT6 behind the TV) vs option B (IPTV smart TV: CAT6 only, "COAX NOT REQ'D"). It turns on whether the procured televisions are smart sets, which is an owner/FF&E decision, not a drawing one. The CAT6 RJ-45 jack is required under both — punch that unconditionally. Do NOT write up a missing coax until the TV question is answered.

THE OPTIONAL DESK-GROMMET DATA OUTLET IS PROVIDED — kn46 is placed on the electrical plan of every first-floor room type and OPTIONAL DATA is a distinct symbol on the legend. "Optional" describes the two delivery methods, not whether to install. What is open is only which method: a real CAT6 jack at the grommet (option A, a genuine ×115 cost item) or just a patch cord from the WAP port (option B). Under either, a guest must get a working wired connection at the desk, so the walker's test is the same.

THE CONNECTED ROOM EDGE CONTROLLER HAS NO MARK, NO LOCATION AND NO SCHEDULE — it is named twice in kn47 and once in E101 GN #8 and appears nowhere else in the set. Consistent with the broader condition: no telecom riser, rack elevation, port count or head-end equipment schedule exists anywhere. The low-voltage package here is effectively owner/vendor-designed, so several rows on this list can only be punched against an integrator submittal rather than against a drawing.

DEVICE BRAND IS NOT LOCKED — E101 GN #2 requires the switch, receptacle, data-tel and TV outlet BRAND be clarified with the franchise and owner before ordering, while E101 GN #8 mandates PANDUIT for the guest-room cable and patch cords with Panduit locks on exposed connections. Those are not contradictory (cable versus outlet device) but they are two different approvals, and a plate or jack that looks wrong at punch may simply be the approved substitution. Confirm the approved device before writing up finish or brand deviations.

NO SECURITY, CCTV OR ACCESS-CONTROL DESIGN EXISTS IN THIS SET (gap LV-5) — those systems are named only in E200 GN #2's "coordinate low-voltage with owner" instruction and in E101's grounding spec. The guest-room card lock on A600 hardware Set #1 is the only lock or access device drawn in a guest room anywhere. If the owner has added in-room sensors, occupancy detection or a networked lock system, none of it is in these documents and none of it is on this list.
